name: Protein crepes (קרפים חלבון) — 2-egg + protein-powder

source.author: Instagram (Hebrew caption)
source.notes: Blender/Ninja protein crepe: ½ a protein drink (or 25–40 g protein powder) + 2 eggs + 2 tbsp flour + a splash of sweetener. Makes 3–4 thin crepes. The post's headline '40 g protein / 440 kcal' ASSUMES you also drink the OTHER half of the protein bottle alongside — so that figure is the crepes PLUS the extra drink, not the crepes alone. Below I give the CREPES-ONLY macros (the batter as cooked) and note the poster's combined figure. Protein-drink macros vary a lot; assumed a ~25 g-protein / ~220 kcal bottle (half in the batter). Tell me the exact shake and I'll tighten it.

serving_desc: the full batch of 3–4 crepes (batter only) as one serving; per-crepe below

ingredients.note: half goes in the batter; the post assumes you drink the other half separately
swap to whole-spelt/oat flour for fiber

steps: Blend the protein, eggs, flour and sweetener smooth (Ninja/blender or whisk well).
Heat a pan, then drop to the LOWEST heat; a touch of oil spray or coconut oil.
Pour a thin layer and tilt to cover the whole pan.
Cover and stay by it — it burns in seconds. When bubbles appear on top, gently free the edges, then flip for ~½ min.
Makes 3–4 crepes depending on pan size.

batch_totals.note: CREPES ONLY (½ shake + 2 eggs + 2 tbsp flour + spray). Per crepe (÷3.5): ~92 kcal, 7.6 g protein, 4 g carb, 3.5 g fat. The post's '40 g protein / 440 kcal' = these crepes PLUS drinking the remaining ½ bottle (~13 g protein / ~110 kcal more).

him.verdict: A genuinely good cut breakfast — ~27 g protein for ~322 kcal in the crepes alone (~8.4 g protein per 100 kcal), driven by 2 eggs plus the protein powder, with very little fat and modest carbs. Eggs also bring selenium and choline. The only real weakness is fiber: 2 tbsp of white flour gives almost none, easily fixed by swapping to spelt/oat flour. The sweetener keeps sugar at zero. If you follow the post and also drink the other half of the shake, you're at the ~40 g protein / ~440 kcal they quote — still a very lean, protein-dense meal.
flags: ~27 g protein / ~322 kcal crepes-only (~8.4 g protein per 100 kcal)
low fiber (~0.5 g) — white flour; swap for whole-grain
poster's 40 g/440 kcal includes drinking the other ½ shake
suggested_mods: Swap the 2 tbsp white flour for whole-spelt or oat flour to add fiber (little macro change)
Top with Greek yogurt + berries for fiber, vitamin C and prenatal micros; or go savory with veg + cheese
Keep the heat genuinely low — protein/egg batter scorches far faster than normal crepe batter

her_preconception.verdict: A strong preconception breakfast IF the eggs are cooked fully through — flip until set, no runny batter (the recipe cooks them through, so it's fine). Eggs are a standout here: ~300 mg choline (key for fetal brain development) plus selenium and protein. Two watch-points: pick a reputable protein powder (not all are third-party tested; some aren't recommended in pregnancy), and non-nutritive sweeteners (stevia/sucralose) are considered safe in normal amounts — moderate if she prefers. Low in folate/iron on its own — the flour swap + a fruit/veg topping fixes that.
prenatal_highlights: choline (~300 mg) + selenium from 2 eggs — fetal brain development
high protein, low fat, fully cooked

safety_advisories.note: Cook the crepes fully through (set, not wet) — standard here, just don't undercook the egg batter.
Use a reputable, ideally third-party-tested protein powder; some aren't recommended in pregnancy. Stevia/sucralose are considered safe in normal amounts.
safety_advisories.swap: a pregnancy-safe protein powder, or extra egg white for protein

suggested_mods: Swap to whole-grain flour and top with fruit/greens for folate, iron + vitamin C
Greek-yogurt + berry topping makes it a well-rounded prenatal breakfast

adopted_note: Adopted 2026-09-25 as a reference (may use in future). Cut-friendly high-protein breakfast: crepes-only ~322 kcal, 27 g protein (~8.4 g protein/100 kcal), ~300 mg choline from 2 eggs. Standing tweak: swap the 2 tbsp white flour for whole-spelt/oat flour to add fiber. Note the post's 40 g/440 kcal assumes drinking the other ½ shake too.
cooking_guide: Blend everything (protein, eggs, flour, sweetener) until completely smooth — a Ninja/blender is ideal; by hand, whisk hard so there are no flour lumps.
Let the batter rest 5–10 min. This hydrates the flour and lets big bubbles settle, giving a more tender, even crepe.
Heat a nonstick pan over medium until hot, then turn it down to the LOWEST setting. Protein + egg batter browns and burns far faster than normal crepe batter — low heat is the whole game.
Add a touch of oil spray or a thin smear of coconut oil. Pour a thin layer of batter and immediately tilt/swirl the pan so it covers the whole surface in a thin, even sheet.
Cover and stay right by it. When the top has set and small bubbles appear and the edges start to lift, gently loosen the edges with a thin spatula.
Flip and cook about another 30 seconds until just set — don't overcook or it turns rubbery.
Stack the finished crepes under a clean towel to keep them soft and pliable.

Tips: thinner batter = lacier, more flexible crepes; a nonstick pan is essential here; for sweet, fill with Greek yogurt + berries or a little nut butter; for savory, skip the sweetener and fill with cheese, egg or veg.
